narrative: Material PL1__ME1021F3 shows erratic demand with a CV of 0.82 and a statistically significant upward trend (p=0.019). Lead times are volatile (CV=0.50, range 0.28–4.28 days), dominated by transport variability. The combined demand and lead-time uncertainty justifies a safety stock of 1,728 units — more than double the current SAP value of 685. An EOQ-based (r,Q) policy replacing the MOQ-driven SAP approach reduces annual costs by 89.6%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but continuous demand with volatile lead times is best served by a continuous-review reorder-point policy. The (r,Q) model sets a fixed reorder point that triggers a fixed order quantity, directly addressing lead-time demand uncertainty without the complexity of variable order sizes.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding: SS (1,728) + OQ (9,291) = 11,019 units < max_storage (13,077). No capacity-driven service degradation expected.
